subject: health
title: Guided practice: dental care
essentialQuestion: How do everyday routines keep my body well and stop germs from spreading?
materials: paper and pencil or an accessible response tool
the fictional lesson cards included in this task
keyPoints: Brush twice a day for about two minutes with a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste.
Brush every surface: outsides, insides, and the chewing tops, plus gently along the gum line.
Sugary drinks sipped slowly over a long time give germs more time to harm teeth than the same drink finished quickly.
Adult teeth grow in around this age and do not get replaced, so caring for them matters.
privacySafeScenario: All required evidence uses fictional or public situations. The learner never has to disclose personal health, body, treatment, feelings, family, sexual, or substance-use information.
studentTask: Write two facts. Use the lesson idea about dental care. Choose one safe next step. Name an adult or help source.
knowledgeCheck: Name the fact. Fix the wrong claim. Choose a safe action. Name who can help.
completionCriteria: I choose a safe action and give a reason.
I name the right kind of help.
adaptationChoices: Show one short direction at a time. Allow reading aloud, word cards, typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking. Help may repeat a direction but may not choose the fact, action, reason, or help source.
extensionChallenge: Create a new fictional or public case about dental care. Include enough facts, choices or constraints, and support authority for another learner to reason safely. Add an accurate explanation of acceptable variation; use no real person's private information.
accessibilitySupports: Show one action at a time.
Offer a vocabulary card and extra time.
Accept typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking for equal credit.
trustedAdultNote: If a real situation feels unsafe or raises a health concern, pause the lesson and tell a parent, guardian, teacher, school staff member, or another trusted adult. A qualified health professional gives medical advice. In an emergency, get an adult and use the local emergency service.

optionalReflection.prompt: Optional and private: Make up one example that helps you remember dental care. Keep it for yourself. You do not need to show it or prove that you completed it.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, body-fat percentage, body comparison, or appearance scoring.
This task never requires calorie counting, dieting, or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires sharing medical history, a diagnosis, treatment, medication, feelings, family conflict, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires advice about an individual learner's treatment, medication, food, supplement, or exercise plan.
standards: Michigan Health Practice 5: Self-Management and Goal Setting
Michigan Health Practice 3: Information and Resource Seeking
Michigan Health Topic (Grades 3-5): Personal Health and Wellness
learningGoal: I can explain dental care, use facts, choose a safe next step, and name who can help.

lessonExperience.privacyNotice: Write only about the made-up people. Keep private information private.

entryCheck.heading: Start with a fact
entryCheck.directions: Choose the sentence that states a fact.
choices: Brush twice a day for about two minutes with a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste.
This one detail proves everything about a person's health.
A popular statement about dental care needs no evidence.
entryCheck.support: A fact is stated in the lesson or supported by reliable evidence. An assumption adds a conclusion the information cannot establish.
entryCheck.treatment: This entry check is unscored. Use the support or prerequisite route before continuing when needed.

explanation.heading: Understand dental care
paragraphs: Brush twice a day for about two minutes with a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste.
Brush every surface: outsides, insides, and the chewing tops, plus gently along the gum line.
Sugary drinks sipped slowly over a long time give germs more time to harm teeth than the same drink finished quickly.
Adult teeth grow in around this age and do not get replaced, so caring for them matters.
explanation.importantDistinction: Learning about dental care supports accurate reasoning and safe next steps; it does not authorize a diagnosis, individualized treatment advice, a person label, or a value judgment.
explanation.decisionRule: PREPARE safely. ORDER the steps. NOTICE the stop point. ASK trained help when the task exceeds your role.

terms.meaning: Brush twice a day for about two minutes with a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste.
terms.boundary: This idea does not diagnose, label, or determine the value of a person.

terms.meaning: facts or reliable evidence that can change the interpretation, choice, or next step
terms.boundary: A guess, popularity, or a personal judgment is not relevant evidence by itself.

terms.meaning: the responsible adult, qualified professional, service, or public authority able to help with the situation
terms.boundary: Naming a support route does not make the learner responsible for diagnosis, treatment, or emergency management.

vocabularyCheck.heading: Check the words
vocabularyCheck.selfCheck: A complete check uses the meaning of dental care, one accurate fact, and the responsible support route without labeling a person.

canonicalPracticeContext.heading: Use the authored practice situation
canonicalPracticeContext.situation: Theo brushes hard and fast for 20 seconds and his gums hurt afterwards. Name two things he could change.
canonicalPracticeContext.treatment: This canonical context may support teaching or discussion. It does not replace the separate fresh independent, mastery, or remediation-retry cases.

modelExample.heading: Watch the reasoning: dental care
modelExample.situation: A fictional Northside class receives mixed-up instruction cards about dental care. The cards include the goal, a safe setup, the lesson fact “Brush twice a day for about two minutes with a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste.”, an action that belongs later, and a stop-and-get-help card. The class must put the safe process in order.
relevantFacts: Brush twice a day for about two minutes with a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste.
Brush every surface: outsides, insides, and the chewing tops, plus gently along the gum line.
modelExample.assumptionOrDistraction: A popular or confident statement about dental care is not automatically accurate and cannot establish a person's health, motives, or character.
possibleActions: Order the safe setup, actions, stop point, and trained-help route.
Begin with the later action and omit the safety check.
Attempt a real procedure beyond current training.
modelExample.successCheck: The model uses the lesson fact, explains the connection, stays within the learner role, and names responsible help when it is needed.
workedReasoning: Start with a safe setup and identify the goal of the procedure.
Put the lesson actions in order and explain why the safety or stop point belongs where it does.
Stop and get trained adult or professional help when the situation is urgent or beyond current training.

guidedReasoning.heading: Try a different case with support
guidedReasoning.situation: A fictional Riverside youth group must explain or act on dental care. The group has this reliable lesson information: Brush every surface: outsides, insides, and the chewing tops, plus gently along the gum line. It has not been given any person's private health information.
availableChoices: Order the safe steps and name the stop point.
Attempt a step beyond current training.
turnOne: Name an adult who can help.
guidedReasoning.cue: Look for the safe setup, correct order, stop point, and trained-help boundary.
feedbackMoves: If a response adds a guess, replace it with a fact from the case or lesson.
If dental care is named without explanation, link one fact to the concept or process.
If a choice is reasonable but the reason is missing, add the fact that supports it.
If a response seeks disclosure, diagnoses, shames, or exceeds the learner role, switch to the fictional facts and the approved help route.
Accept an equivalent typed, handwritten, drawn-and-labeled, signed, selected, or spoken response when it shows the same reasoning.
guidedReasoning.turnTwo: Fix one sentence. Use a fact and a safe next step.
guidedReasoning.releaseCondition: Continue when the response uses a stated fact, applies dental care, and gives a safe next step without private disclosure or a person label.

independentEvidence.heading: Show what you know on a fresh case
independentEvidence.situation: A fictional Maple Community Center has an unordered set of steps for dental care. The information card says: Brush twice a day for about two minutes with a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste. Create the safe order, identify a stop point, and name when trained adult or professional help takes over.
directions: Use the lesson idea about dental care.
Name an adult or help source.
permittedSupports: read-aloud or one direction at a time
typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking
independentEvidence.independenceBoundary: Support may restate a direction or provide access. It may not choose the controlling fact, conclusion, action, reason, safety judgment, or help route.
successCriteria: I choose a safe action and give a reason.
I name the right kind of help.

freshMasteryCheck.heading: Check the idea in a new place
freshMasteryCheck.situation: A fictional Lakeside school committee reviews dental care. The committee knows: Sugary drinks sipped slowly over a long time give germs more time to harm teeth than the same drink finished quickly. It must correct one unsupported claim and choose a safe next step.
freshMasteryCheck.freshnessNote: This case is different from the model, guided case, and independent case. Do not copy their conclusions.

remediation.heading: Try a different model
remediation.trigger: Use this route after an observable gap in a fact, vocabulary meaning, reasoning step, process order, or help route for dental care.
remediation.prerequisite: First restate this approved fact in your own words: Brush twice a day for about two minutes with a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste.
remediation.alternateExplanation: Use a path map with four signs: SET UP, DO IN ORDER, STOP IF, and GET HELP. The map separates a classroom description from a real action that requires trained supervision.
contrast: Sufficient: uses a stated fact about dental care, explains the connection, and stays within the learner role.
Needs revision: repeats a topic word, adds a guess, or gives an action with no factual reason or responsible help source.
remediation.guidedCorrection: Cross out the guess. Circle the fact. Add one safe action.

freshRetry.situation: A fictional Oak Street library receives a new question about dental care. Staff provide this approved fact: Brush every surface: outsides, insides, and the chewing tops, plus gently along the gum line. The learner must respond without using the Northside, Riverside, Maple, or Lakeside conclusions.

remediation.exitCriterion: Return to the independent route when the learner accurately uses a fact, applies dental care, explains a safe response, and identifies support without answer-bearing help.
remediation.nextRoute: If the same gap remains, return to the named prerequisite with an adult instructor; do not replace the task with private reflection.

laterTransfer.timing: Use in a later lesson or a separate session.
laterTransfer.prompt: Apply dental care to a meaningfully different fictional or public case. Retrieve the concept, use relevant facts, justify a safe response, and identify the responsible support or authority route.
laterTransfer.masteryBoundary: The current independent response is one evidence occasion. Mastery requires accurate independent evidence now and accurate later retrieval or transfer.

contentProvenance.objective: Practice dental care with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support.
